title: company.json v0.1
description: Machine-readable conformance aid for the company.json specification, version 0.1 Draft. The specification prose is normative; if this schema and the specification conflict, the specification governs (Spec §4). Rules this schema cannot express are listed in the top-level $comment.
$comment: NOT ENFORCED BY THIS SCHEMA (validators must implement separately, per Spec §4): duplicate raw JSON property names (§7.3, requires raw-input inspection); host binding and redirect authorization (§11); URL reachability (§12.5); uniqueness of contact `type` values across the contacts array (§9.9, JSON Schema uniqueItems only rejects fully identical objects); alternateNames repeating the value of `name` (§9.5, no cross-property reference); mutual-declaration evaluation (§9.10.2); the 1 MiB size floor (§7.2); leading/trailing whitespace warnings (§12.4, SHOULD-level); HTML markup detection in human-readable values (§9.6 and §12.4, requires an HTML parser or documented heuristic); all other SHOULD-level guidance. FORMAT ASSERTION: RFC 3339 date/date-time validity (e.g. rejecting February 30) and IRI syntax require a validator configured to assert recognized formats, or equivalent application-level semantic checks; under the standard Draft 2020-12 dialect, `format` is annotation-only by default.

specVersion.description: Specification version this document conforms to. Spec §9.1.

name.description: Primary public name of the organization. Spec §9.2.

url.description: Canonical public website. Used for host binding (Spec §11). Spec §9.3.

legalName.description: Registered or formal legal name. Spec §9.4.

alternateNames.description: Other recognized names. SHOULD NOT repeat `name` (not schema-enforceable). Spec §9.5.

description.description: Concise first-party description. MUST NOT contain HTML markup; HTML detection requires an application-level semantic check. Spec §9.6.

logo.description: URL of the preferred official logo. One logo in the v0.1 core. Spec §9.7.

sameAs.description: Official organization profiles hosted by other services. URLs only in v0.1. Spec §9.8.

contacts.description: Public contact channels. At most one entry per `type` (§9.9; array-level uniqueness of `type` is NOT enforced by this schema - see top-level $comment).

relationships.description: Declared relationships to other organizations or brands. Duplicate relationship objects SHOULD be reported as warnings, not rejected (Spec §12.6), so uniqueItems is deliberately NOT asserted here; strict mode may enforce it. Spec §9.10.

brandResources.description: URL of an official brand, press, or media-resource page. Spec §9.11.

lastUpdated.description: RFC 3339 full-date or date-time of the last meaningful profile update. Patterns are asserted because `format` is annotation-only in draft 2020-12. Spec §9.12.

extensions.description: Namespaced non-core data. Keys MUST be an absolute URI (any scheme, e.g. https:, urn:, did:) or a reverse-domain-style name with >=2 dot-separated labels, no leading/trailing hyphens. Values may be any JSON. Spec §9.13.

httpUrl.$comment: Absolute HTTP(S) IRI. The authority component may not contain '@' (no embedded credentials, Spec §12.5) or whitespace. `format` is annotation-only in draft 2020-12, so the pattern is asserted; validators should additionally assert the `iri` format (note: `iri` support varies across validators — application-level IRI checking is an acceptable substitute). Schemes are case-insensitive per RFC 3986; strict mode may warn on non-lowercase schemes.

email.$comment: SHOULD be a plain address, not a mailto: URL (§9.9). SHOULD-level, so not pattern-enforced here; strict mode may reject 'mailto:' prefixes.

contact.$comment: MUST include at least one of email, telephone, url (§9.9). A contact of type 'other' MUST include a non-empty name (§9.9).

relationship.$comment: Reciprocity evaluation (§9.10.2) is consumer behavior, not document validity, and is not expressed here.
